Danielle —

Thanks, and appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a proposal PDF and an editable ramp workbook (see attachments). Summary below; full numbers in attachment: quantalign-dedicated-proposal-20261021.pdf.

Proposal highlights (summary):
- Pricing model: committed tokens/month + throughput SLAs. Price shown as $/M tokens for predictable billing.

Option A — 12 months:
- Committed: 200M tokens / month
- Unit price: $6.20 per M tokens
- Upfront discount: 5% on list for 12-month prepay
- Ramp: 0–2 months 40% of committed, month 3–6 linear to 100%

Option B — 24 months (recommended):
- Committed: 180M tokens / month (volume discount factored)
- Unit price: $5.00 per M tokens
- Contract-level discount: 18% off list spread across term
- Ramp: 0–3 months 35% starting coverage, automatic accelerators if usage exceeds committed tiers (see workbook)

Option C — 36 months:
- Committed: 160M tokens / month
- Unit price: $4.55 per M tokens
- Additional credit: 1 month invoice credit if start delayed >45 days and caused by Redwood

Throughput & SLA:
- Baseline throughput guarantee: 75K tokens/sec aggregate for the dedicated pool (measured as 95th percentile over 5-minute windows).
- Penalty credits: 5% of monthly invoice per SLA miss (capped at 20% per month) after 3 consecutive misses.

Start-window / delay policy (summary):
- If Redwood cannot deliver committed capacity by the agreed start date +30d, QuantAlign receives pro-rated credits on the monthly invoice for the period of shortfall.
- For delays >60d, we offer either: (a) one free month of service (credit) on 24/36m deals or (b) an option to extend the ramp by equivalent time without additional charge.

Attachments: quantalign-dedicated-proposal-20261021.pdf; capacity-ramp-schedule-quantalign.xlsx (editable).

2) Share any procurement redlines and SOC2 evidence requests; we'll loop Security to provide the packet.
3) We will prepare a DocuSign package once terms are agreed.

Cc'ing Karthik for operational acceptance criteria and Dev for technical ramp notes.

Danielle / Aisha —

Quick operational note on the ramp workbook: the throughput guarantee (75K tokens/sec) scales with the pool if you select the accelerator clause. Practical implications: if during month 2 you hit >110% of the committed tokens consistently, our autoscaling policy will provision burst nodes to preserve latency SLOs; those burst nodes bill at a marginal rate (shown in sheet 'BurstPricing').

I also want to highlight an intermediate staging option: if QuantAlign needs an earlier partial start, we can provision a smaller GPU pool (staging pool) with a short-term premium (15% uplift) and then roll into the dedicated commit once full capacity is ready. This often helps teams that have hard production launch dates but uncertain procurement timing.

I'll attach a short operational checklist in the Drive folder for your infra team. We recommend the following acceptance test window: 72 hours of steady-state traffic at >90% of target throughput before we flip traffic to the dedicated pool.

-Dev
